name: Panchadha Maitri (Five-Fold Planetary Friendship) Grades
note: The 5 combined grades of Panchadha Maitri (Naisargika/natural + Tatkalika/temporal friendship) - the GENERIC meaning of each grade, applicable to any pair of the 7 classical grahas. The actual natural-friendship table and the temporal-friendship computation (which needs each planet's real house position in a specific chart) live in code, not here - see engine/maitri.py - since Tatkalika Maitri is chart-dependent and can't be pre-computed into a static KB file the way the grade meanings below can. This file is the counterpart to planet_in_sign.json's dignity-status text (exalted/own/debilitated/neutral): dignity describes a planet's relationship to the SIGN it's in; Panchadha Maitri describes its relationship to whichever planet actually LORDS that sign (or to any other planet it's being compared against) - a separate, additional layer of strength/weakness, not a replacement for dignity.

verification_pass.method: The natural-friendship table in engine/maitri.py (not this file) was checked row-by-row against a classical BPHS-derived reference table and passes an internal self-consistency assertion (every planet's row covers the other 6 grahas exactly once, no omissions or duplicates) that runs automatically on import. The 5 grade-meaning texts here were cross-checked for consistency with each other (grade severity ordering) and with how dignity-status text in planet_in_sign.json is worded, so the two layers read as complementary rather than contradictory.

items.title: Great Friend (Adhi Mitra)
items.summary: Natural friend and temporally well-placed — the warmest possible relationship between two planets.
items.effects: Both the permanent (Naisargika) and the chart-specific (Tatkalika) friendship point the same way here, so a planet sitting in a Great Friend's sign is considered a welcome, supported guest: its significations tend to express with unusual ease, and it lends genuine strength to whatever it governs. Classically the strongest of the five Panchadha Maitri grades.

items.title: Friend (Mitra)
items.summary: Naturally neutral, but favorably placed in this chart — a working friendship, not an inborn one.
items.effects: The two planets have no fixed natural bond, but their positions in THIS particular chart bring them into a cooperative relationship. A planet placed in such a sign is a comfortable, if not especially close, guest — its expression is generally supported without being amplified.

items.title: Neutral (Sama)
items.summary: The natural and temporal readings pull in opposite directions and cancel out.
items.effects: Either a natural friendship undercut by an unfavorable chart position, or natural dislike offset by a favorable one — the two effects balance each other. A planet here is neither especially helped nor hindered by its host; read its other dignities (exaltation, own sign, etc.) as the more decisive factor.

items.title: Enemy (Shatru)
items.summary: Naturally neutral, but unfavorably placed in this chart.
items.effects: No inborn hostility, but this chart's specific arrangement puts the two planets at odds. A planet placed in such a sign is a somewhat unwelcome guest — its expression can feel constrained or effortful, without being as severely undermined as under a Great Enemy.

items.title: Great Enemy (Adhi Shatru)
items.summary: Natural enemy and temporally poorly placed — the most difficult of the five grades.
items.effects: Both the permanent and the chart-specific reading agree: this is real friction. A planet sitting in a Great Enemy's sign is considered an unwelcome guest in hostile territory — its significations tend to express with real difficulty, and classical texts treat this as a meaningful weakening factor, on top of (not instead of) whatever exaltation/own-sign/debilitation status already applies.
